title: Spanish
description: Learn everyday Spanish: greetings, numbers, food, family and getting around.

units.title: Greetings
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
units.tip: Use 'buenos días' until lunchtime, 'buenas tardes' in the afternoon and early evening, and 'buenas noches' late in the evening or to say good night.

units.title: Introductions
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
units.tip: 'Tú' is the informal 'you'. Accents matter in writing: 'tú' (you) and 'tu' (your) are different words.

units.title: Being polite
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
units.tip: Spanish questions start with an upside-down question mark (¿) and exclamations with (¡). You do not need to type them here.

exercises.prompt: Excuse me, do you speak English?

exercises.translation: Excuse me, do you speak English?

units.title: Numbers 1–10
units.description: Numbers, food and drink, and talking about your family.
units.tip: 'Uno' becomes 'un' before a masculine noun (un libro) and 'una' before a feminine noun (una manzana).

units.title: Food and drink
units.description: Numbers, food and drink, and talking about your family.
units.tip: 'Me gusta' literally means 'it pleases me'. Spanish usually keeps the article: 'Me gusta el café' = 'I like coffee'.

units.title: Family
units.description: Numbers, food and drink, and talking about your family.
units.tip: The masculine plural can cover mixed groups: 'hermanos' can mean 'brothers' or 'brothers and sisters'.

units.title: Getting around
units.description: Travel basics, ordering at a café, and days of the week.
units.tip: 'Billete' is used in Spain; in much of Latin America a ticket is a 'boleto'.

units.tip: 'Zumo' is used in Spain and 'jugo' in Latin America. Both are accepted.

units.title: Days and time
units.description: Travel basics, ordering at a café, and days of the week.
units.tip: Days of the week are not capitalised in Spanish. 'El lunes' means 'on Monday'.
